title: Exploring Structural Degradation in Dense Representations for Self-supervised Learning
mechanism: Longer SSL training can degrade dense-task performance. A label-free Dense representation Structure Estimator (class relevance + effective dimensionality) selects checkpoints or regularises training.
adaptation: Only useful alongside a D32 pool SSL run (159k pool, new backbone): score SSL checkpoints with DSE on pool cells and fine-tune from the DSE-chosen one, not the last.
min_experiment: Arm: PF fine-tune from the DSE-selected SSL checkpoint. Baseline: PF fine-tune from the last checkpoint. Metric: val + F51 crack AP, then test crack IoU. Kill: DSE choice no better than the last checkpoint on val.
evidence: R: degradation seen across 16 SSL methods; DSE-based model selection gives +3.0 mIoU on average at negligible cost.
prior_overlap: Partial. MIM and DDeP pool pretraining were n.d., always using the final checkpoint; checkpoint selection was not tested.
